videos.script: A VLAN keeps two departments apart. Sooner or later they need to talk. The warehouse needs the file server in the office VLAN, and everybody needs the printers. {{apart}} A switch cannot do that on its own. Each VLAN is its own subnet, and between subnets you need a router. {{router}} In this lesson you will give the lab a router with a single cable, plugged into a trunk. One port, and one address in each VLAN. The design is called router on a stick. {{stick}} You will watch one ping cross that cable four times, and see why the cable becomes the limit. {{twice}} Then you will unplug the router and move the routing into the switch itself. That is a layer 3 switch. The first ping after the move fails, and you will see exactly why. {{switch}} Next you will use the router's position to filter. One VLAN may reach a web server in the other, and nothing else. {{filter}} Last, a broken trunk, and a checklist that finds the fault in the order the packet travels. {{check}}
